a student assessment system must have: (1) A clear and well-articulated purpose, (2) A clear and coherent architecture, (3) A sound technical foundation, (4) Adequate capacity, and (5) Adequate resources.

a well functioning student assessment system is one that is (1) designed to meet the needs of students, schools, and the education system as a whole, (2) based on sound principles of good assessment practice, and (3) implemented with adequate resources and sustained over time.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how to build a system of student assessment that: - provides information that is useful for improving learning and achievement; - is valid, reliable, fair, and efficient; - provides information that supports accountability for results and is useful for improving teaching; - is affordable and sustainable; - provides a sound basis for tracking and monitoring progress and for making policy decisions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the following are what matters most for a student assessment system: * The system should be based on the national curriculum, with the assessment system designed to provide evidence of what students have learned and achieved against the curriculum standards.

what matters most for student achievement is the quality of the education system as a whole, including the quality of the teachers, the quality of the curriculum, and the quality of the learning materials.

a well designed and implemented assessment system can provide a wealth of data to support decision making, but that the quality of the data and the quality of the decisions made are dependent on a range of factors, many of which are not directly related to the assessment system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
student learning assessment is not a technical exercise, but rather an important and complex policy decision.
the following matters most: * Student assessment is an integral part of the teaching and learning process and is a critical element in the overall quality of education system.
the key to effective student assessment is the quality and coherence of the system, not the individual components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are no silver bullets in the assessment arena, but there are many good ideas and approaches that can be adapted and used to create a more effective assessment system.
a well-designed and well-functioning student assessment system can play an important role in improving education quality.
there is a lot to learn from countries' experience and from research about how to build a more effective student learning assessment system.
